limitations: sourcePagesChecked lists pages of the current question PDF only; supplementary comparator pages are identified separately in scope and findings.

The 2020 positive comparator and key establish the accepted old-paint/rust pair and reject the two filler combinations, but do not supply the reason for either filler-group mismatch or their accepted replacements.

3M practical guidance supports DA paint removal and feather edging and distinguishes filler shaping, glaze sanding and subsequent refinement. It does not identify the JASPA textbook grouping or establish a one-to-one equivalence between its material categories and the examination terms.

No false universal inability claim is identified in the revised DA caveats. HOLD concerns the missing educational rationale for choices (3) and (4), not an answer-key discrepancy or a demand to invent exclusive real-world tool uses.
No candidate, product, prior receipt or commit was changed. Report prose is ASCII; field labels use JSON Unicode escapes.

findings.issue: Choice (3) still restates rejection by the official key, followed by sound but generic tool-selection advice. Neither inspected examination identifies which member or material/stage assignment makes the straight/orbital/DA combination inappropriate for the stated polyester-putty category. Thus the learner cannot derive the intended correction independently of memorizing the key.
findings.replacement: Retain official answer (2) and the practical caveat. Pending evidence, state explicitly: The official key rejects this combination, but the exact textbook mismatch has not yet been established. To complete the explanation, obtain the applicable JASPA textbook edition/page, official worked rationale, or a positive comparator establishing the relevant correct grouping; identify the specific misplaced tool or category and give the supported replacement. Do not infer that any listed machine is universally incapable of sanding polyester putty.

findings.issue: The positive rotary-plus-disc mapping for paint/rust does not establish an exclusive use or show why rotary/disc/DA is the wrong body-filler grouping. Flatness and finish quality are relevant considerations, but the present explanation does not connect them to a source-supported mismatch in this option. The 2020 comparator repeats this rejected combination and therefore provides no positive filler-group correction.
findings.replacement: Retain the supported paint/rust mapping and the statement that DA body-filler sanding is not universally prohibited. Explicitly label the body-filler grouping rationale as unresolved until an applicable textbook passage, official worked explanation or positive comparator identifies the intended correction. Then state the particular tool/category mismatch and supported correct grouping or stage-specific distinction. Do not treat a tool being appropriate for paint removal as proof that it is excluded from filler work.
